output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe specification (what/where/when) to localize the fault, then competing-hypotheses weighing, then a source check on the exit survey and the VP's email.
output.brief: The buffering in Kestria is almost certainly caused by the new smart-TV app version 5.2, not the CDN switch. From 12–25 October, smart-TV 5.2 stalled 5.9% of the time. Every other client, including the web player and phone apps, stalled about 0.6–0.7% on the same Tessaline CDN. This held on all three ISPs. The jump started on 9 October, the day the app released and the day of the cutover, so the timing alone could not separate them. Handball match nights were no worse than other days, so extra demand isn't the cause. Do not send the SLA breach notice, withhold fees, or move traffic back. That would not fix the problem and would penalise the wrong party. Do not mute the alert. Instead, revert the 5.2 adaptive-streaming behaviour in Kestria and hold the wider rollout until it is fixed. Then watch whether rebuffering falls. Treat the link to cancellations as unproven. The 1 October price rise is a competing explanation, and the exit survey has no quality option. A free-month offer based on buffering is premature. Adding app-version breakdowns to the dashboard is worthwhile but needs about six weeks. Confidence is high on cause and moderate on the cancellation link.
